html:
The Miluk were a Coosan-speaking people of the southern Oregon coast, around the South Slough of Coos Bay and the mouth of the Coquille River. Their language, Miluk, was one of two Coos languages; the other was spoken by their Hanis neighbours around the main bay.

They fished, gathered shellfish and lived in plank houses. Settlers and gold miners arrived in the 1850s, and after the Rogue River Wars of 1855 to 1856 the Coos peoples were held on the coast reservation. One of the last Miluk speakers, Annie Miner Peterson, dictated stories and songs to the linguist Melville Jacobs in 1933, and these keep much of what is known of the language. Miluk descendants belong to the Confederated Tribes of Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw and the Coquille Indian Tribe.
